Engine component · optimization

Fewer tokens. Same proof.

Optimization is one stage of the governed-context engine — it distills a verified pack to the smallest form that still answers the task, and ships three tiers so you trade cost against detail on purpose. The rule that makes it safe: token reduction is not success unless fidelity survives. Source handles, citations and held-out warnings carry through every tier — compression never deletes the proof.

Tokens to answer “What’s the Reg E error-resolution deadline?”
⚠ A token win that drops a citation or a held-out warning is a regression, not an optimization. Baltor’s verification rail re-checks the optimized pack and fails it if a source handle or contradiction was lost — efficiency never overrides provenance.
